$comment: Poderators run a Pod through a Build Cycle (the app calls them shepherds; the name isn't settled). The button is given once trained and seated. Placeholders: hours a week, the training, and the sign-up link.

meta.need: As someone who met a person wearing the poderator button, I need to know who they are and how to think of them, so that I can trust what they told me.

description: A Poderator keeps a Pod of nine or more people together through a Build Cycle at The Upskilling Labs, from the first meeting to the Showcase.

title: Keep the Pod
moving.
hero.alt: The Poderator button: the orb mark on ink, ringed by THE UPSKILLING LABS and PODERATOR

intro.lede: Every Pod in a Build Cycle has a Poderator: the person who keeps a Pod of Upskillers together and moving, from the first meeting to the Showcase. You don't have to be the expert. You make sure everyone gets there.
intro.terms: One Pod, one Build Cycle: about three months, busiest at the start and the end.
intro.status: Poderators are chosen before each Build Cycle begins

met.$comment: For someone who met a wearer and wants to know who that was and how to think of them (most people who land here). The lede doubles as the spoken line the role's training gives wearers, so the page and the person say the same thing (design/research/role-explainers.md).
met.lede: They're a Poderator. They keep a Pod of nine or more people together through a Build Cycle, from the first meeting to the Showcase.

know.title: A volunteer.
know.body: Looking after one Pod, for one Build Cycle.

know.title: Not the teacher.
know.body: Mentors bring the know-how. The Poderator makes sure everyone gets there.

know.title: A role, not a certification.
know.body: The button says what they're doing this cycle.

met.where: You'd meet one at a Pod meeting, a workshop at the public library, or the Showcase. Ask them what their Pod is working on.

items.title: Gather the Pod.
items.body: They run the check-ins and the in-person events, and help everyone find their footing.

items.title: Keep it moving.
items.body: When a team stalls, they ask the question that gets it going, or bring in a Mentor.

items.title: Get them to the Showcase.
items.body: They watch the Pod show what it built.

items.title: One Pod at a time.
items.body: One Pod, for one Build Cycle.

items.title: Trained first.
items.body: You're seated once you've done the Poderator training.

items.title: Questions over answers.
items.body: You keep the Pod moving. Mentors bring the know-how.

items.title: Free, always.
items.body: Nothing to pay, and nothing to sell.

path.title: You hold the room. The Pod does the rest.

steps.title: Create your account.
steps.body: Your free Upskilling account: sign in with Google, and tell us you'd like to run a Pod.

steps.title: Get trained.
steps.body: There's nothing to qualify for before you start. You train for the role and run your first Pod alongside someone who's done it.

steps.title: Take your seat.
steps.body: You're seated for a Build Cycle and get your Poderator button.

steps.title: Do it again.
steps.body: Run another Pod next cycle, and help train the next Poderators.

button.title: The one to find.
button.body: Worn at every Pod meeting and library event, so Upskillers know who to ask. It marks a role, not a certification.

items.q: Do I need to be an expert?
items.a: No. You keep the Pod together and moving. Mentors bring the expertise.

items.q: How much time does it take?
items.a: One Build Cycle: twelve weeks, busiest at the start and the end.
Yes. There's nothing to qualify for before you start: you train for the role, run your first Pod alongside someone who's done it, and earn your way to running Pods on your own by doing it well.
Not really. There's no curriculum to get through. Teams work on a real problem and learn what they need along the way.

join.title: Run a Pod with us.
join.lede: It starts with your free Upskilling account. Then tell us you'd like to run a Pod.
